opening: We make choices every day, often without considering how one decision leads to another. But what happens when we recognize what is right and choose not to act upon it?
body:
In today's Gospel, Jesus asks a question that seems so simple, yet carries a powerful warning:

“Why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?” — Luke 12:57

Jesus points to something we all understand. We recognize the signs of changing weather. We see clouds gathering and know rain is coming. We feel the wind shift and anticipate the heat.

Yet Jesus calls the crowd hypocrites because, despite their ability to interpret the world around them, they fail to recognize what is happening spiritually before their eyes.

God was present among them in Christ, and still they struggled to see.

I wonder how often we do the same.

We have been given the ability to recognize right from wrong, yet sometimes we ignore what we know to be true. We justify our actions, delay difficult decisions, or wait for someone else to tell us what we should already recognize within ourselves.

Jesus then speaks of settling with an opponent before reaching the judge.

At first, this sounds like a warning about punishment. But I believe there is also mercy in His words.

We are still on the way.

Every moment brings a choice, and each choice influences the moments that follow. If we hold ourselves accountable for what we choose today, we begin establishing the standards by which we will live tomorrow.

That does not mean we will always choose correctly. We are human, and we will stumble. But even then, we have another opportunity to recognize our mistakes, seek forgiveness, and return to what is right.

In today's first reading, Paul urges us to live with humility, gentleness, patience, and love. These are not simply virtues to admire. They are choices we must practice, especially when doing so is difficult.

Perhaps Jesus' warning is not only about the judgment that awaits us, but about the responsibility we have while there is still time.

We cannot know what tomorrow will bring, but we can examine our hearts and take responsibility for how we live today.

God does not ask us to know everything that lies ahead. He asks us to recognize what is right and have the courage to act upon it.

And when we fail, His mercy gives us the opportunity to begin again.
prayer: Lord Jesus,  Help me recognize what is right, even when it is difficult to accept.  Give me the humility to examine my own actions before judging those of others, and the courage to correct my mistakes rather than justify them.  Holy Spirit, guide the choices I make today so that my life may grow in patience, gentleness, and love.  And when I lose my way, remind me that Your mercy is still calling me back.  Amen.
theme: Every choice is an opportunity to recognize what is right and live accordingly.
title: What Does Your Gut Tell You?
